clue.text: Position of flyer uncertain

definitions.meaning: where a bird or pilot is while flying: aloft, overhead
an idiom for undecided, still not settled

explanation.surface: Someone is unsure where a pilot or a bird currently is.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not yet decided is said idiomatically to be still hanging aloft, unsettled; literally, a flyer is aloft.

clue.text: Billy Joel's type of girl — high-class platinum individual

parts.note: U is the old British label for upper-class usage
Pt is the chemical symbol for platinum
own as in one's own, particular to oneself

explanation.surface: A pop fan describes the girl in a Billy Joel song as a posh, precious individual.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Joel's 1983 hit is 'Uptown Girl', about a rich, well-bred young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Joel's song title names a smart-district girl, so the adjective from the title fits the blank.

clue.text: Communicate monkey culture

parts.note: a mischievous child is called a monkey or an imp
the arts are culture

explanation.surface: A zoologist passes on findings about how apes learn behaviour from one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monkey' here is the playful word for a naughty child, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on news or knowledge to someone is a synonym for conveying or telling it.

clue.text: Reversing routine with kid, she cooked low-calorie sweet

indicators.note: reversing tells us to turn the word for routine around

parts.note: a rut is a dull routine

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of kid and she have been worked over into a new order

parts.note: light foods are low in calories

explanation.surface: A mother breaks her routine and cooks a diet dessert with her child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' makes KISHDE from KID and SHE; 'Reversing' turns RUT into TUR.
explanation.definitionFit: This rose-flavoured jelly cube dusted in sugar is a classic confection, an example of a sweet.

clue.text: Film duck eating edge of sandwich in Scottish town

indicators.note: eating means the duck's name takes the rest inside it

parts.note: the eider is a sea duck

indicators.note: in places the sandwich's outer letter inside the town's name

parts.note: Ayr is a town on the Ayrshire coast of Scotland

indicators.note: edge of takes the outermost, starting letter of sandwich

explanation.surface: A duck in a Scottish town pecks at a sandwich crust, like a scene from a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' at the front looks like a verb; it is the definition, a 1969 road movie. 'edge of' gives S, which goes 'in' the town to make ASYR before the duck is 'eating' it.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1969 road movie with Peter Fonda and Dennis Hopper is a famous American picture.

clue.text: How foreign footballer introduces himself, dodging English press?

indicators.note: dodging means the English letter is avoided, left out

parts.note: the Brazilian star Pelé would say '...é'

explanation.surface: A foreign player at a press conference introduces himself while avoiding English.
explanation.walkthrough: IM PELE loses one E to give the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To press someone into action is to urge or drive them forward, a synonym.

clue.text: Some earache from Gordon Ramsay perhaps

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people get a pain in the ear from Gordon Ramsay's famous shouting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramsay is a celebrity cook running restaurant kitchens, an example of the profession.

clue.text: Greek underworld suspiciously nice

parts.note: hell is the underworld of the dead

indicators.note: suspiciously suggests the word nice is not what it seems and its letters have been tampered with

explanation.surface: The Greek underworld, Hades, seems oddly pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspiciously' rearranges NICE into ENIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is the formal term for things belonging to Greece or its people.

clue.text: Some of plane passengers finally entering incite anger, being topless

indicators.note: entering means the chosen letter goes inside the word for incite

parts.note: to fuel unrest is to incite it

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of passengers
topless means the word loses its top, its opening letter

parts.note: rage is anger

explanation.surface: Airline passengers become angry, perhaps over a topless fellow traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: S enters FUEL to make FUSEL; 'being topless' cuts RAGE down to AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of an aircraft is one part of it, so the main body is 'some of' a plane.

clue.text: Don't say what dentist might do when drilling

definitions.meaning: an order to keep quiet, keep something to oneself

definitions.text: what dentist might do when drilling
definitions.meaning: a dentist may literally keep the patient's tongue out of the way of the drill

explanation.surface: A patient in the chair is told not to speak while the dentist drills.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells someone to stay silent; a dentist might also literally keep the mouth's muscle out of the way.

clue.text: Casual instruction where to record vocal animal?

indicators.note: vocal says the instruction is spoken, so we want what it sounds like

parts.note: an informal 'tape 'ere' tells someone to record at this spot

explanation.surface: A sound recordist wants to capture the call of a noisy animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the H, as in casual London speech, makes 'tape here' into 'tape 'ere'.
explanation.definitionFit: The snouted hoofed mammal of the Americas and Malaysia is a kind of beast.

clue.text: Dramatist who's cited in divorce perhaps caught during scrapes

parts.note: SOP is short for significant other person, someone who might be named in a divorce

indicators.note: during means the letter for caught is in the middle of the word for scrapes

parts.note: being in a hole is being in a scrape, so holes are scrapes
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A playwright is named in a divorce case after being caught in a series of scrapes.
explanation.walkthrough: SOP, a significant other person, is an obscure abbreviation; the blogger congratulated anyone who got it from the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian tragedian who wrote Oedipus Rex and Antigone is one of the great playwrights.

clue.text: Combatant Irish artist in argument gets backing

indicators.note: gets backing means the whole assembly is read from the back
in places the abbreviations for Irish and artist inside the argument

parts.note: a row is an argument
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An Irish painter, in the middle of a quarrel, finds people supporting him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets backing' turns the whole of ROIRRAW round, not just one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter or soldier is someone who engages in combat, a synonym.

clue.text: British Olympian covering some French centre of excellence

parts.note: a lid covers a pot
de is French for some, as in du pain

indicators.note: centre of takes the middle pair of letters of excellence

explanation.surface: A British athlete is protected by a French training academy.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric Liddell was the Scottish runner who won gold at the 1924 Paris Olympics, the hero of Chariots of Fire.
explanation.definitionFit: The 400m champion of 1924 competed for Great Britain, so he is an example of a British Olympian.

clue.text: How Hank Marvin etc warmed up?

definitions.text: How Hank Marvin etc warmed up?

parts.words: How Hank Marvin etc warmed up?
parts.note: Hank Marvin played guitar in The Shadows, Cliff Richard's backing group, so the band might warm up like a boxer sparring with no opponent

explanation.walkthrough: Hank Marvin was lead guitarist of The Shadows, a British instrumental band of the 1960s; boxers warm up by sparring with no opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparring against an imaginary opponent is a boxer's warm-up, punned onto the Shadows' band name.

clue.text: Female group, inserting dish, cooked gran a symbol of the North

parts.note: the WI, the Women's Institute, is a British women's organisation

indicators.note: inserting means the dish is put inside the scrambled word
cooked suggests gran's letters have been stirred up into a new order

parts.note: a pie is a dish

explanation.surface: At the Women's Institute, Gran bakes a pie, the very image of northern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' makes GANR from the grandmother's word, and 'inserting' puts the dish in its middle. The Lancashire landmark became famous through George Orwell's book The Road to Wigan Pier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lancashire landmark, made famous by Orwell, stands as an emblem of industrial northern England.

clue.text: Handsome youth, for example swapping Dolce & Gabbana, initially struggled

indicators.note: the initial letters of the fashion house's two names change places in the assembled word

parts.note: Adonis was the beautiful youth of Greek myth

explanation.surface: A handsome young model battled after Dolce & Gabbana were swapped for another label.
explanation.walkthrough: ADONIS plus EG gives ADONISEG; the D and G trade places.
explanation.definitionFit: To have agonised is to have wrestled painfully over something, a synonym for struggled.

clue.text: Infringe principle of expenses till company begin to operate a check

parts.note: principle puns on principal, the chief or leading part: the leading letter of expenses
NCR, National Cash Register, is a firm famous for making tills

indicators.note: begin to takes the opening letter of operate

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: An accounts clerk explains expense rules before a cash-register firm starts running an audit.
explanation.walkthrough: NCR is National Cash Register, a maker of shop tills.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude on someone's rights or territory is to trespass upon them, a synonym for infringe.

clue.text: Spice Girl received by second dancer

parts.note: Geri Halliwell was Ginger Spice in the Spice Girls
roger is radio speak for message received

explanation.surface: A Spice Girl is welcomed in by a backing dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spice Girl' looks like a kind of spice; it is Ginger Spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Astaire's screen partner was a celebrated Hollywood hoofer, an example of the art.

clue.text: Learning to stuff a daily piece of broccoli

indicators.note: to stuff means the word for learning is packed inside the newspaper

parts.note: the FT, the Financial Times, is a daily paper
lore is learning, traditional knowledge

explanation.surface: Someone uses a newspaper to stuff a piece of broccoli, as a learning exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: A small flowering head of a vegetable such as cauliflower is a branchlet, one piece of it.

clue.text: Rum's operating price

definitions.note: the answer is a betting term used as an adjective or noun for a short price

parts.note: rum means odd, and the 's stands for is, giving odd's
a machine that is operating is on

explanation.surface: A bar owner talks about how much a bottle of rum costs to run.
explanation.definitionFit: In horse racing, a starting price shorter than evens is described this way, so it names a betting price.

clue.text: Somewhere in UK and not the Caribbean or Switzerland

parts.note: nor means and not
WI is the West Indies, the Caribbean islands
CH is Switzerland's international code

explanation.surface: A traveller lists a destination: it is in Britain, not in the Caribbean or Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: Norwich is a cathedral city in Norfolk, in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norfolk city is a place in Britain, so it is an example of somewhere in the UK.

clue.text: Soul star, on Sky, partnered him?

definitions.text: Soul star, on Sky, partnered him?

parts.words: Soul star, on Sky, partnered him?
parts.note: David Soul played the detective partnered by Starsky, whose name is STAR plus SKY read together

clue.text: Old one, moving close to band, played intricate solo?

indicators.note: moving says the letters are shifted about into a new arrangement
close to takes the closing letter of band

explanation.surface: An old band member, moving to the front, plays a complex solo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges OLDONE plus D, the end of 'band'.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise a meandering, fiddly passage on an instrument is slang for playing a fancy solo.

clue.text: Food brought back … it affected the passages

indicators.note: affected suggests the letters of it and the are disturbed into a new order

explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' gives SPAG from GAPS; 'affected' rearranges IT and THE into HETTI.
explanation.definitionFit: These long thin pasta strings are an Italian staple, an example of food.

clue.text: Jewellery clasping tip of finger is a source of infection

definitions.note: the answer is plural, the definition singular; microbes collectively are a source

indicators.note: clasping means the jewels hold the letter inside them

parts.note: gems are jewellery

indicators.note: tip of takes the end letter of finger

explanation.surface: Rings gripping a fingertip may harbour bacteria.
explanation.walkthrough: The tip here is the last letter of 'finger', R, not its first.
explanation.definitionFit: Microbes such as bacteria and viruses cause disease, so they are where infections come from.

clue.text: Herald cryptic evades pausing novelist

indicators.note: cryptic suggests the letters of Herald are mysteriously jumbled

parts.note: er is the sound of someone pausing in speech

explanation.walkthrough: 'evades' takes ER out of HERALD, leaving HALD, which 'cryptic' rearranges.

clue.text: Cleaner lets loose on steps

parts.note: a char, or charwoman, is a cleaner

indicators.note: loose says the letters of lets are set free to go into a new order

explanation.surface: A cleaner lets herself loose on the staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a British word for a cleaning lady. 'loose' makes LEST from LETS.
